**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is part of an ongoing multi-session technical writing and book production project called "The Method 1.6." The person is the author of a six-volume work in progress and is directing Claude through a structured build process across numbered chat sessions (this being chat 13, Rebuild 13). The project involves a main volume, a Register compendium (1,447 headings covering 1,472 distinct entry numbers, range 165–1768, non-contiguous), and four additional compendia. Work is organized around numbered "BUILD" bundles stored in project knowledge, with all editorial and production records kept in a separate `WORKING-REGISTER.md` that never enters the books (per Ruling 27). Rulings 27 and 28 plus a Ruling 27 Amendment are in force, governing the separation of subject-matter content from editorial work and the absorption of two external papers as Chapters 35 and 36, fixing the deliverable set at six volumes.

The session had one substantive accomplishment and one significant correction. The accomplishment was Task 1: closing five surviving instances in the main volume of language referencing three removed register audits (GRAPH, CYCLE, NOMENCLATURE) and incorrect audit counts of "twenty-five" that should read "twenty-two." This included repairing an orphan predicate left by a prior session's incomplete edit. The repair was executed with assertion-guarded content matching, verified clean (GRAPH/CYCLE/NOMENCLATURE at zero occurrences in main), and recorded as W-001 in `WORKING-REGISTER.md`. The citation repair (Task 2, 28 entries across 66 sites) was measured and fully mapped but not started. BUILD-14 bundles (2 + 67 members) were produced and round-trip verified.

The significant correction came when the person stated that `guard.py` does not exist and was never in any bundle — it was built after chat 11 and then deleted when that line of sessions was abandoned and restarted from chat 11. The person identified this as the recurring fatal flaw of every session since chat 11: work begins before the full prior chat record is read, causing Claude to act on directive text rather than the actual file record. The person explicitly instructed that all required reading must be completed at the start of every session before any work is done. In response, HANDOFF-15 was structured with a mandatory §0 reading gate — four enumerated steps ending in a printed certificate — with its failure mode explicitly written into the handoff so the gate can actually fail rather than existing only as a practice clause. The handoff also explicitly lists tools named in directives that do not exist (`guard.py` and six others), with the operative rule: a directive naming a tool is not evidence the tool exists.

**Tool Knowledge**

The `/mnt/project` mount syncs with a delay; a file confirmed present by the person was not visible in an early `ls` listing taken several minutes before the sync completed. When a bundle appears absent, the correct response is to re-list rather than treat absence as confirmed — this project's bundles are large and sync slowly. The pattern `re.finditer(r"^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)\n?<<<END FILE: \1>>>", text, re.S|re.M)` reliably splits both bundle formats used in this project. Register entry headings must be parsed with `r"^### ([\d,\s]+?)\s*$"` and grouped headings explicitly expanded via `re.findall(r"\d+", m.group(1))`; a naive `^### (\d+)` parse misses seven grouped headings carrying 32 numbers and produces phantom citation classes. The BUILD-12 vs BUILD-13 Register diff (isolating chat 12's excisions from pre-existing gaps) is the correct basis for classifying dead citations as Class A (repair required) versus Class B (pre-existing, separate matter); without that diff the two classes are conflated. Round-trip verification after bundle packing — re-parsing each output bundle and comparing extracted content against source files — is required before declaring a bundle current.

def split(bundle, outdir):

import re
def parse(txt):
    single=set(); grouped={}
    for m in re.finditer(r"^### ([\d,\s]+?)\s*$", txt, re.M):
        nums=[int(x) for x in re.findall(r"\d+", m.group(1))]
        if len(nums)==1: single.add(nums[0])
        else: grouped[nums[0]]=nums
    return single, grouped
new=open("The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md",encoding="utf-8").read()
s,g = parse(new)
allnums=set(s)
for k,v in g.items(): allnums.update(v)

print("naive '^### N' count (what the book prints):", len(re.findall(r"^### (\d+)", new, re.M)))
print()
print("sample grouped headings:", list(g.values())[:8])
EOF
